title: ROC curve
text: Sweep the cutoff from strict to loose and track how many home wins the model catches against how many false alarms it raises. The closer the curve hugs the top-left corner the better. Area under it (AUC) is 0.84; a coin flip is 0.50.

title: Precision vs recall
text: Same sweep, different trade-off: asking for more home wins caught (right) usually costs picks that are less often correct (up). The dashed line is what guessing 'home' every time would score, so the gap above it is real skill.

title: Can you trust the percentages?
text: Games are grouped by the chance the model gave them. Dots on the dashed line mean 70% really did win about 70% of the time. Dots below the line mean the model is overconfident in the home team there; above means underconfident.

title: Right and wrong picks
text: Counts of games by what the model picked and what happened. The diagonal is correct picks (77% of games). Off-diagonal boxes are the misses: top-right is a false alarm for the home team, bottom-left is a home win it missed.

title: How well the percentages separate winners
text: Predicted home win chance for games the home team won (blue) and lost (orange). A model that separates well pushes blue to the right and orange to the left. Heavy overlap in the middle is the honest picture: most halftime games are not settled yet.

title: What the cutoff changes
text: Calling 'home' at 50% is a choice. Raise the cutoff and the model picks home less often: precision and specificity rise while recall falls. Lower it and the reverse happens. The dashed line is the 50% cutoff used in the accuracy table.

title: What each input is worth
text: Each dot says by what factor the home team's odds of winning get multiplied when that input rises by one typical amount. Right of 1 helps the home team, left of 1 hurts it. A bar crossing 1 means the effect could be zero.

title: Which inputs the model leans on
text: Scramble one input so it carries no information and measure how much the probabilities degrade. Long bars are inputs the model needs. A bar near zero means the input barely matters.

title: What happens as one input changes
text: Blue is the average home win chance as one input slides across its range with everything else left alone; gray lines are individual games. The S-shape is the logistic curve: the same extra point matters most when the game is close and less once it is nearly decided.

title: Would more data help?
text: Orange is the error on games the model trained on; blue is the error on games it had not seen. Lines that flatten and sit close together mean more seasons would add little. A wide gap would mean the model memorizes its history.
